title.en: Reported Speech — Direct to Indirect Made Easy
title.hi: Reported Speech — Direct se Indirect Easy Tarike Se

headline.en: Reported Speech — Reporting What Someone Said
headline.hi: Reported Speech — Kisi ne kya kaha, usse Report Karna

text.en: One mental picture makes Reported Speech click forever — plus the exact 2 situations where tense should NOT change.
text.hi: Ek mental picture Reported Speech ko hamesha ke liye click kara degi — plus wo 2 exact situations jahan tense change NAHI hona chahiye.

content.en:
What is Reported Speech?

Reported Speech mein kisi aur ke words ko apne words mein batate hain. Inverted commas ("") hatakar 'that' lagate hain.

Direct: He said, "I am tired."
Indirect: He said that he was tired.

4 Steps to Convert:
1. Change reporting verb (said → said/told/asked)
2. Remove commas & inverted commas → add 'that'
3. Change pronouns (I → he, my → his, etc.)
4. Backshift tense (Present → Past)
content.hi:
Reported Speech kya hai?

Reported Speech mein kisi aur ke words ko apne words mein batate hain. Inverted commas ("") hatakar 'that' lagate hain.

Direct: He said, "I am tired."
Indirect: He said that he was tired.

4 Steps to Convert:
1. Reporting verb change karo (said → said/told/asked)
2. Commas aur inverted commas hatao → 'that' lagao
3. Pronouns change karo (I → he, my → his, etc.)
4. Tense backshift karo (Present → Past)

content.en:
🚗 Imagine You're the Only One Retelling the Story Later

Here's the mental picture that makes Reported Speech click: imagine your friend said something to you at school this morning, and now it's evening and you're telling your mom about it at home.

Everything that was 'close' when it was said is now 'far away' by the time you're retelling it:
• The moment ('now') has moved into the past → becomes 'then'
• 'Today' has passed → becomes 'that day'
• The word 'here' (school) is a different place now (home) → becomes 'there'
• Your friend's 'I' is not you → becomes 'he/she'

This is the ENTIRE logic of Reported Speech in one sentence: everything shifts one step further away in time, place, and person — because you're no longer in that original moment.
content.hi:
🚗 Socho Tum Akele Baad Mein Ye Story Retell Kar Rahe Ho

Ye mental picture Reported Speech ko click kara deti hai: socho tumhare friend ne school mein aaj subah kuch bola, aur ab shaam ho gayi hai aur tum ghar pe mummy ko wo baat bata rahe ho.

Jo bhi 'paas' tha jab bola gaya tha, wo ab retell karte waqt 'door' ho jaata hai:
• Wo pal ('now') ab past mein chala gaya → 'then' ban jaata hai
• 'Today' guzar gaya → 'that day' ban jaata hai
• 'here' (school) ab ek alag jagah hai (ghar) → 'there' ban jaata hai
• Tumhare friend ka 'I' tum nahi ho → 'he/she' ban jaata hai

Yehi Reported Speech ki POORI logic hai ek sentence mein: sab kuch time, place, aur person mein ek step aur door shift ho jaata hai — kyunki tum ab uss original moment mein nahi ho.

content.en:
Step 1: Reporting Verb Changes

Said → Said / Told / Asked / Ordered / Requested

• 'Said to' → 'told' (jab object ho)
  - Direct: He said to me, "I am busy."
  - Indirect: He told me that he was busy.

• Questions → 'asked' / 'inquired' / 'wondered'
  - Direct: He said, "Are you coming?"
  - Indirect: He asked if/whether I was coming.

• Commands → 'ordered' / 'requested' / 'advised'
  - Direct: He said, "Open the door."
  - Indirect: He ordered me to open the door.

Memory Trick: Sentence ki feeling ke hisaab se reporting verb choose karo.

content.en:
Step 2 & 3: Pronoun & Time/Place Changes

Pronoun Changes:
| Direct | Indirect |
|---|---|
| I | he/she |
| we | they |
| you | I/he/she |
| my | his/her |
| our | their |
| me | him/her |
| us | them |

Time & Place Changes:
| Direct | Indirect |
|---|---|
| now | then |
| today | that day |
| tomorrow | the next day |
| yesterday | the previous day |
| here | there |
| this | that |
| these | those |
| ago | before |

Memory Trick: Speaker ke perspective se sab door ho jata hai → 'this' becomes 'that', 'now' becomes 'then'.

content.en:
Step 4: Tense Backshift (Sabse Important)

Jab reporting verb PAST mein ho → tense ek step peeche jaata hai:

| Direct Tense | Indirect Tense |
|---|---|
| Simple Present | Simple Past |
| Present Continuous | Past Continuous |
| Present Perfect | Past Perfect |
| Present Perfect Cont. | Past Perfect Cont. |
| Simple Past | Past Perfect |
| Past Continuous | Past Perfect Continuous |
| will | would |
| can | could |
| may | might |
| must | must / had to |

Exception: Universal truth ya habitual action mein tense NAHI badalta!
• Direct: He said, "The sun rises in the east."
• Indirect: He said that the sun rises in the east. (NO change)

Jab reporting verb PRESENT/FUTURE mein ho → tense same rehta hai:
• Direct: He says, "I am busy."
• Indirect: He says that he is busy. (NO change)

content.en:
Questions, Commands & Exclamations

YES/NO Questions:
• 'said' → 'asked' + if/whether
• Direct: He said, "Are you coming?"
• Indirect: He asked if/whether I was coming.

WH-Questions:
• 'said' → 'asked' + WH-word
• Direct: He said, "Where are you going?"
• Indirect: He asked where I was going.

Commands (Order):
• 'said' → 'ordered/commanded/told' + to + V1
• Direct: He said, "Sit down."
• Indirect: He ordered me to sit down.

Requests:
• 'said' → 'requested/begged' + to + V1
• Direct: He said, "Please help me."
• Indirect: He requested me to help him.

Exclamations:
• 'said' → 'exclaimed' / 'wished' / 'prayed'
• Direct: He said, "What a beautiful flower!"
• Indirect: He exclaimed that it was a beautiful flower.

content.en:
🥊 Confusion Buster — When Tense Does NOT Change

Students backshift EVERY tense automatically — but there are 2 situations where the tense must stay exactly as it was:

Situation 1: Universal truths / facts that are always true
• He said, "The sun rises in the east." → He said that the sun rises in the east. (NOT 'rose' — a fact doesn't become less true in the past)

Situation 2: The reporting verb itself is Present or Future
• He says, "I am busy." → He says that he is busy. (reporting verb 'says' is present, so no backshift needed)

Quick test before backshifting: Ask 'Is this a fact that's always true?' or 'Is the reporting verb (said/says) actually in past tense?' If either answer breaks the usual pattern, don't backshift.
content.hi:
🥊 Confusion Buster — Kab Tense Change NAHI Hota

Students HAR tense ko automatically backshift kar dete hain — but 2 situations hain jahan tense bilkul same rehna chahiye:

Situation 1: Universal truths / hamesha sach baatein
• He said, "The sun rises in the east." → He said that the sun rises in the east. ('rose' NAHI — ek fact past mein kam sach nahi ho jaata)

Situation 2: Reporting verb khud Present ya Future mein hai
• He says, "I am busy." → He says that he is busy. (reporting verb 'says' present hai, isliye backshift ki zaroorat nahi)

Backshift se pehle quick test: Poocho 'Ye ek fact hai jo hamesha sach hai?' ya 'Reporting verb (said/says) actually past tense mein hai?' Agar dono mein se koi bhi usual pattern todta hai, backshift mat karo.
